name: IANA Root Zone Database
note: IANA operates the root zone, so this is the authoritative list of top-level domains
rather than anyone's copy of it. Which strings are delegated is a matter of fact, not
authorship, so `public-facts` records that reasoning rather than asserting a grant
The digest deliberately ignores the leading `# Version` serial. IANA republishes this
file with a fresh serial whenever the zone is regenerated, whether or not a TLD
changed -- it moved from 2026080600 to 2026080700 with all 1,438 entries identical.
Pinning the raw bytes failed the build daily for no reason, and a check that cries
wolf every morning is one everybody learns to bypass. Every line that becomes corpus
data is still covered, so a TLD appearing, disappearing or being injected still fails.
`version` records the serial seen when the content was last verified, and is
transcribed rather than read back out of the file. Reading it was tried and was
self-contradictory: the digest ignores the serial precisely because it changes
without the data changing, and then the version adopted the very same number --
so every rebuild on a new day produced a different provenance chunk, a different
blob and a stale locale module, for a zone that had not moved. A number that
changes when the data does not is not a version of the data.
